mainTopic: Mixed intent in a קרבן פסח: one עבודה or two, a פסח slaughtered during the year with לשמו ושלא לשמו, and שינוי בעלים during the year
overview: The amud opens by finishing an attempt to answer רב פפא's question: is the משנה's case of mixed intent about one עבודה or two? The גמרא tries to prove it from the סיפא, but rejects the proof, so that question is not settled here. Next comes an איבעיא about a פסח slaughtered during the rest of the year with both לשמו and שלא לשמו intent. רב דימי argues it is פסול by comparing it to ערב פסח, but רבי ירמיה rejects his comparison. רבא then rules that it is כשר: since שלא לשמו can override the default לשמו status, it can also override a spoken לשמו. רב אדא בר אהבה challenges this from the case of לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו. רבא answers that a פסח has no fixed default group of eaters, because people may join or withdraw until the שחיטה. Finally, a new איבעיא asks whether שינוי בעלים during the year makes a פסח כשר the way שינוי קודש does. רב פפא says yes, and רבא begins to reject that comparison, an answer that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof from the latter clause that the first clause is about one rite
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא argues that since the סיפא must be about one עבודה, the רישא must also be about one עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't the latter clause about one rite? And since the latter clause is about one rite, the first clause must also be about one rite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is trying to answer רב פפא's question by comparing the two clauses of the משנה. It says that because the second clause is clearly about a single עבודה, the first clause must be too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא (intent for people who can eat and people who cannot) is כשר even when both intents happen in one עבודה. The גמרא assumes both clauses of the same משנה speak about the same kind of case. If so, the רישא (לשמו ושלא לשמו, which is פסול) is also about one עבודה, which would show that the end of a person's statement counts, like רבי יוסי.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, is it not that... (introduces the conclusion the גמרא wants to prove)
One sacrificial rite (for example, only the שחיטה)
The latter clause of the משנה
The first clause of the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Here the רישא means the mixed-intent case of לשמו ושלא לשמו, which is פסול. The סיפא means the case of eaters and non-eaters, which is כשר. Don't mix up which clause is which.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about one rite?
phrases.notes: Concluding the analysis of the סיפא from the previous discussion.

phrases.english: And since the latter clause is about one rite,
the first clause is also about one rite!
phrases.notes: So the רישא would follow רבי יוסי: even the end of one's words counts.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִדְּסֵיפָא בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת רֵישָׁא נָמֵי בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier attempt (on the previous amud) to answer רב פפא's question from the משנה.
steps.raayaObject: That the רישא (לשמו ושלא לשמו, פסול) speaks of one עבודה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The parallel structure of the סיפא, which is about one עבודה

steps.title: Rejection: the two clauses need not be about the same kind of case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that each clause can be explained on its own terms, so the proof fails and רב פפא's question stays open.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that a valid comparison?! This one is as it is, and that one is as it is. The latter clause is about one rite, and the first clause may be about either one rite or two rites.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 1. It says there is no rule that both clauses must describe the same kind of case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא may be about one עבודה, but the רישא could be a broader statement that covers both one עבודה and two עבודות. Because of this, we cannot learn from the רישא whether the end of a statement counts. רב פפא's question is left without a clear answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that comparable?! (a phrase used to reject a comparison)
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is (each case stands on its own)
Two separate rites (for example, שחיטה and זריקה)

steps.whatToRemember: The attempt to prove from the משנה whether the case is one עבודה or two is rejected. The רישא might cover both possibilities, so רב פפא's question stays unresolved.

phrases.english: Are these comparable?!
This one is as it is, and that one is as it is.
The latter clause is about one rite,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֵישָׁא אוֹ בַּעֲבוֹדָה אַחַת, אוֹ בִּשְׁתֵּי עֲבוֹדוֹת.
phrases.english: and the first clause is about either one rite or two rites.
phrases.notes: So nothing can be proven from the רישא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִידֵּי אִירְיָא הָא כִּדְאִיתָא וְהָא כִּדְאִיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in Step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the סיפא to the רישא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It wrongly assumes both clauses of a משנה must describe the same kind of case. The רישא may be broader.

steps.title: New question about mixed intent for a Paschal lamb during the year
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים ask whether a פסח slaughtered during the year with both לשמו and שלא לשמו intent is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: A פסח that was slaughtered during the rest of the year both for its own sake and not for its own sake, what is its status? Does the 'not for its own sake' intent come and remove it from 'for its own sake' and make it valid, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question. Outside ערב פסח, the rules flip: שלא לשמו makes a פסח valid (as a שלמים), and לשמו makes it invalid. The question is what happens when a person has both intents at once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח, לשמו validates a פסח and שלא לשמו disqualifies it. During the rest of the year it is the opposite: a פסח slaughtered שלא לשמו becomes a valid שלמים, while one slaughtered לשמו is פסול. The question asks whether the validating intent (שלא לשמו) cancels the disqualifying intent (לשמו) when both are present.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was asked of them (an open question among the חכמים)
The rest of the days of the year (any time other than ערב פסח)
For its own sake (with intent that it is a פסח)
Not for its own sake (with intent for a different offering)
Makes valid

steps.confusionAlert: Outside ערב פסח the usual roles flip: here שלא לשמו is the GOOD intent and לשמו is the BAD intent.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered during the rest of the year
for its own sake and not for its own sake, what is its status?
Does the 'not for its own sake' intent come
and remove it from the status of 'for its own sake'
and make it valid, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, still dealing with mixed intent in a קרבן פסח.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a validating שלא לשמו intent cancels a disqualifying לשמו intent for a פסח slaughtered outside ערב פסח.

steps.title: רב דימי compares the year to ערב פסח: mixed intent is disqualified
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי reports his reasoning before רבי ירמיה: just as לשמו does not cancel שלא לשמו on ערב פסח, שלא לשמו does not cancel לשמו during the year, so the animal is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב דימי came, he said: I said this teaching before רבי ירמיה: Since לשמו makes it valid in its proper time, and שלא לשמו makes it valid outside its proper time, then just as לשמו, which makes it valid in its time, does not remove it from שלא לשמו, so too שלא לשמו, which makes it valid outside its time, does not remove it from לשמו, and it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רב דימי answers the question by comparing two situations. He sets up each intent as the 'valid-making' intent in its own season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On ערב פסח, a mix of לשמו (good) and שלא לשמו (bad) is פסול, because the good intent does not cancel the bad. רב דימי says the year works the same way: the good intent (שלא לשמו) does not cancel the bad intent (לשמו). So mixed intent during the year is also פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: When רב דימי came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)
Since
In its proper time (ערב פסח)
Just as... so too... (a comparison formula)
Invalid, disqualified

steps.whyThisMatters: This is only רב דימי's proposed reasoning. רבי ירמיה rejects it in step 5, and רבא rules the opposite in step 7: during the year, mixed לשמו ושלא לשמו is כשר. Do not take this step as the halacha.

phrases.english: When Rav Dimi came, he said:
I said this teaching before Rabbi Yirmeya:
Since 'for its own sake' validates it in its proper time,
and 'not for its own sake' validates it outside its proper time:
just as 'for its own sake,' which validates it in its time,
does not remove it from 'not for its own sake,'
phrases.notes: On ערב פסח, mixed intent is פסול.

phrases.aramaic: אַף שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ הַמַּכְשִׁירוֹ שֶׁלֹּא בִּזְמַנּוֹ —
phrases.english: so too 'not for its own sake,' which validates it outside its time,
does not remove it from 'for its own sake,' and it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי אֲתָא רַב דִּימִי אָמַר אַמְרִיתָא לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in Step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The animal is פסול: the validating intent (שלא לשמו) does not cancel the disqualifying intent (לשמו), just as on ערב פסח לשמו does not cancel שלא לשמו.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה rejects רב דימי's comparison
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה tells רב דימי that his comparison fails. On ערב פסח, שלא לשמו is a problem for every קרבן. During the year, לשמו is only a problem for the פסח, so it is weaker and can be cancelled.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to me: No! You can say that about 'not for its own sake,' because that problem applies to all offerings. But can you say the same about 'for its own sake,' which is a problem only for the פסח and no other offering?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ירמיה pushes back on the reasoning רב דימי presented in step 4. He says the two cases are not equal, so the comparison cannot be used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי argued: on ערב פסח, לשמו does not cancel שלא לשמו, so during the year שלא לשמו should not cancel לשמו. רבי ירמיה answers that שלא לשמו is a strong problem because it applies to all זבחים. 'לשמו at the wrong time' is a weak problem that applies only to the פסח, so a weak problem might be cancelled even though a strong one is not.

keyTerms.meaning: Animal offerings (sacrifices)
Applies / is in effect
Only, alone
'Will you say?', used to reject a comparison

phrases.english: And he said to me: No!
phrases.notes: רב דימי is quoting רבי ירמיה's reply.

phrases.english: If you said this about 'not for its own sake'
phrases.notes: This refers to the ערב פסח case.

phrases.english: that is because it applies to all offerings,
will you say it about 'for its own sake'
phrases.notes: This refers to the case during the year.

phrases.english: which does not apply to all offerings
but only to the פסח alone?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the comparison רב דימי made in step 4.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רב דימי's reasoning that the year-round case mirrors the ערב פסח case.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The two invalid intents are not equally strong. שלא לשמו disqualifies all זבחים, but לשמו during the year only matters for the פסח.

steps.title: So what is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Now that רב דימי's reasoning has been rejected, the גמרא asks what the final law is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the conclusion about it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the bottom-line ruling on the question from step 3, which is still open.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב דימי's reason for calling the animal פסול was knocked down. So the question goes back to the beginning, and the גמרא asks for a ruling. The answer will come from רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'What is the conclusion about it?', asking for a final ruling

phrases.english: What is the conclusion about it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the דחיה, the גמרא returns to the open question from step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The final law for a פסח slaughtered during the year with both לשמו and שלא לשמו intent.

steps.title: רבא rules the animal is valid
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that it is כשר. By default, a פסח stands as לשמו, yet slaughtering it שלא לשמו makes it כשר. So שלא לשמו pushes aside לשמו, and the same should happen when both are said.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: A פסח slaughtered during the rest of the year, both for its own sake and not for its own sake, is valid. Here is why. By default it stands as 'for its own sake.' Even so, when someone slaughters it 'not for its own sake,' it is valid. This shows that 'not for its own sake' comes and removes it from 'for its own sake.' So also, when he slaughters it both for its own sake and not for its own sake, the 'not for its own sake' comes and removes it from 'for its own sake.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives the final answer: the animal is כשר. He proves it from the simple case where someone slaughters a פסח during the year שלא לשמו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: During the year, a פסח slaughtered לשמו is פסול, but one slaughtered שלא לשמו (for example, as a שלמים) is כשר. Even though the animal is still a פסח by default, saying שלא לשמו is enough to override that default. So רבא reasons that שלא לשמו also overrides an explicit לשמו, and the animal is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Its default state, with nothing specified
Stands, is in that status
'Apparently / this shows that', introducing an inference
Takes it out of (a status)
The rest of the days of the year (not ערב פסח)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't flip the rules! During the year, a פסח slaughtered לשמו is the PROBLEM (פסול). Slaughtering it שלא לשמו is what makes it כשר. That is the reverse of ערב פסח.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: during the year, mixed לשמו and שלא לשמו is כשר, because שלא לשמו overrides even the default לשמו status.

phrases.english: Rava said:
A Paschal lamb that one slaughtered during the rest of the year
for its own sake and not for its own sake is valid.
For by default it stands as 'for its own sake',
phrases.notes: It is still a פסח unless something changes it.

phrases.english: and even so,

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שָׁחֵיט לֵיהּ שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ — כָּשֵׁר,
phrases.english: when he slaughters it not for its own sake, it is valid,
this shows that 'not for its own sake' comes
and takes it out of 'for its own sake'.

phrases.aramaic: כִּי שָׁחֵיט נָמֵי לִשְׁמוֹ וְשֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ —
phrases.english: So also when he slaughters it for its own sake and not for its own sake,

phrases.aramaic: אָתֵי שֶׁלֹּא לִשְׁמוֹ וּמַפֵּיק לֵיהּ מִידֵי לִשְׁמוֹ.
phrases.english: 'not for its own sake' comes and takes it out of 'for its own sake'.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: פֶּסַח שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ בִּשְׁאָר יְמוֹת הַשָּׁנָה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: כשר. שלא לשמו overrides the default לשמו, so it also overrides an explicit לשמו.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: a spoken intent may differ from a default
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה challenges רבא's proof. Overriding a default status does not mean you can override something actually said. He proves this from לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא בר אהבה said to רבא: Maybe a case where he said it is different from a case where he did not say it. For if he slaughters it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, it is valid. But whenever he slaughters it only for those who cannot eat it, it is invalid. Why? By default it stands for those who can eat it! Rather, a case where he said it is different from a case where he did not say it. Here too, a case where he said it is different from a case where he did not say it!
steps.whatsHappening: רב אדא בר אהבה attacks the proof behind רבא's ruling. He argues that a default status (not spoken) is weaker than an intent that is actually spoken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With people who can eat the פסח, an explicit 'for eaters' saves the animal even if 'non-eaters' is added. But the default 'for eaters' does not save an animal slaughtered only for non-eaters. So the default is weaker than a spoken intent. In the same way, שלא לשמו may override a default לשמו without overriding a spoken לשמו, and then רבא's proof fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, introducing a possible rejection
It is different
For those who are registered and able to eat it
Alone, by itself
And why? (asking for the reason)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea about intent: an explicit מחשבה can be stronger than a default status, so proofs from default cases do not automatically carry over to spoken ones.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said to Rava:
Perhaps a case where he said it is different
from a case where he did not say it.
For if he slaughters it for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it, it is valid,
but wherever he slaughters it
only for those who cannot eat it, it is invalid,
and why? By default it stands for those who can eat it!

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שָׁאנֵי הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר מֵהֵיכָא דְּלָא אָמַר.
phrases.english: Rather, a case where he said it is different from a case where he did not say it.

phrases.aramaic: הָכִי נָמֵי, שָׁאנֵי הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר מֵהֵיכָא דְּלָא אָמַר!
phrases.english: Here too, a case where he said it is different from a case where he did not say it!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה לְרָבָא: דִּילְמָא שָׁאנֵי הֵיכָא דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the proof רבא used in step 7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: רבא's proof, which compares a default לשמו to a spoken לשמו.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A default status is weaker than a spoken intent, as the לאוכליו case shows. So overriding a default does not prove you can override something actually said.

steps.title: רבא shows the two cases are different
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רב אדא בר אהבה. A פסח's default status is surely לשמו, but its default status is not לאוכליו.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Are these cases really alike? Granted, there, as long as he did not uproot it at the time of slaughter, by default it certainly stands as for its own sake. But here, does it by default stand for the people who will eat it?!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא defends his proof by showing that רב אדא's comparison to לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא said that overriding a default status is weaker than overriding something actually said. רבא answers that in the case of לאוכליו there is no real default at all, so that case proves nothing. With לשמו, the default is real and certain, so it is fair to compare a default to an actual statement.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (a formula rejecting a comparison)
Granted, it makes sense in that case
Uprooted (cancelled the status by an explicit intention)
Its default state, when nothing is said
For those registered to eat it

steps.confusionAlert: Who is speaking? This is רבא, answering רב אדא בר אהבה's challenge from step 8. It is not רב אדא continuing his own point.

phrases.english: He (Rava) said to him: Are these comparable?
Granted, there (regarding for its own sake)
as long as he did not uproot it at the slaughter
by default it certainly stands as for its own sake.
But here (regarding its eaters)
does it by default stand for its eaters?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב אדא's counter-proof from step 8 and restores רבא's proof from step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases (חילוק): one has a real default, the other does not.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Overriding a default can never be compared to overriding an explicit statement, as לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו shows.
steps.terutzMaskana: לאוכליו has no default status, so it proves nothing. לשמו has a certain default, so רבא's comparison stands.

steps.title: Why a פסח has no default group of eaters
steps.stepSummary: The registered eaters can withdraw and others can join, as a משנה teaches, so a פסח has no fixed default of לאוכליו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps these people will withdraw, and others will come and register for it. As we learned in a משנה: People may register for it and withdraw their hands from it, until it is slaughtered.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains his point from step 9 and backs it up with a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until the moment of slaughter, the group of eaters can still change. So you cannot say the animal 'automatically' stands for any particular eaters. That is why only an explicit statement of לאוכליו counts, and why that case cannot be used against רבא's proof.

keyTerms.meaning: They withdraw (pull out of the group)
They register (join the group for the קרבן)
As we learned in a משנה
They register and withdraw

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's proof survives: a פסח stands as לשמו by default, so שלא לשמו overriding that default shows it can also override an explicit לשמו. The final ruling is that the animal is כשר.

phrases.english: perhaps these will withdraw
and others will come and register for it,
(others) as we learned in a mishna:
phrases.notes: The parenthetical word appears in the printed text and is likely a scribal repetition.

phrases.english: they may register and withdraw their hands from it,
until it is slaughtered.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains and proves the claim in step 9 that there is no default of לאוכליו.
steps.raayaObject: A פסח has no fixed default status of לאוכליו.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה: נמנין ומושכין את ידיהם ממנו עד שישחט.

steps.title: Question about a פסח slaughtered for the wrong owner during the year
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if a פסח is slaughtered during the year with שינוי בעלים, does it become כשר like it does with שינוי קודש?
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: A פסח that someone slaughtered during the rest of the year with a change of owner, what is the law? Is a change of owner like a change of sanctity, so that it makes the animal valid, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question and sets up רב פפא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a פסח slaughtered during the year as a different קרבן (שינוי קודש) is כשר as a שלמים. The question is whether intending it for a different owner (שינוי בעלים) works the same way and also makes it כשר, or whether it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them (an open question)
The rest of the days of the year (not ערב פסח)
Change of owner: slaughtering it for someone other than its owner
Change of sanctity: slaughtering it as a different type of קרבן
Makes it valid (כשר)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two changes. שינוי קודש means the wrong type of קרבן. שינוי בעלים means the right קרבן for the wrong person.

phrases.english: A dilemma was raised before them:
A Pesach that one slaughtered on the rest of the days of the year
with a change of owner, what is the law?
Is a change of owner like a change of sanctity
and so it validates it, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question after the לשמו/שלא לשמו discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does שינוי בעלים during the year make a פסח כשר, the way שינוי קודש does?

steps.title: רב פפא compares a change of owner to a change of sanctity
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא argues that since both changes disqualify a פסח in its proper time, both should make it כשר after its time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: I said this teaching in front of רבא: Since a change of sanctity disqualifies it in its proper time, and a change of owner also disqualifies it in its proper time, then just as a change of sanctity, which disqualifies it in its time, makes it valid after its time, so too a change of owner, which disqualifies it in its time, makes it valid after its time.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers the question from step 11 by comparing the two kinds of change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two changes share one feature: each one makes a פסח פסול on ערב פסח. רב פפא reasons that they should also share the opposite result during the year, where שינוי קודש is known to make it כשר. So שינוי בעלים should also make it כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: I said this teaching
Since
In its proper time (ערב פסח)
After its proper time (the rest of the year)
Disqualifies it

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next part of the סוגיא, where the comparison between שינוי בעלים and שינוי קודש will be examined.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
I said this teaching before Rava:
Since a change of sanctity disqualifies it in its time,
and a change of owner disqualifies it in its time,
just as a change of sanctity, which disqualifies it in its time,
validates it after its time,
so too a change of owner, which disqualifies it in its time,
validates it after its time.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא, אַמְרִיתָא לִשְׁמַעְתָּא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: שינוי בעלים during the year makes the פסח כשר, just like שינוי קודש, because both disqualify it in its proper time.

steps.title: רבא rejects the comparison: a change of sanctity is a stronger disqualification
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא reports that רבא rejected his comparison. שינוי קודש is a more serious פסול than שינוי בעלים, because it damages the offering itself and applies in all ארבע עבודות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he (רבא) said to me: No! If you said this about a change of sanctity, that is because its disqualification is in the offering itself, and it applies to all four services.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is rejecting רב פפא's argument that שינוי בעלים should work like שינוי קודש. He starts by listing two ways that שינוי קודש is stronger, and the contrast with שינוי בעלים continues right on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's argument depended on the two changes being equal, since both make a פסח פסול in its proper time. רבא shows they are not equal. שינוי קודש changes what the offering itself is (פסולו בגופו), and it can happen during any of the four main services, not only at שחיטה. So the fact that שינוי קודש makes a פסח כשר during the year does not prove the same for the weaker שינוי בעלים.

keyTerms.meaning: "No! If you said...": a standard formula for rejecting a comparison by showing the first case has a special strength
Change of sanctity: slaughtering an offering as a different type of קרבן
Its disqualification is in its body: the problem lies in the offering's own identity, not in something outside it
The four main services of a קרבן: שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה, זריקה
Change of owners: slaughtering the offering for someone other than its owner

steps.confusionAlert: This passage ends in the middle of רבא's answer. רבא has not yet finished his point. The next words explain that שינוי בעלים lacks both of these strengths.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that two kinds of פסול that look alike (both disqualify a פסח in its time) can still differ in strength. A comparison built only on their shared result can therefore fail.

phrases.english: And he said to me: No!
phrases.notes: רב פפא is reporting רבא's reply to him.

phrases.english: If you said this about a change of sanctity —
phrases.notes: Here שינוי קודש means slaughtering the פסח as a different קרבן.

phrases.english: that is because its disqualification is in its body,
phrases.notes: This is the first strength: the change affects the offering's own identity.

phrases.english: and it applies to all four services,
phrases.notes: This is the second strength: it can disqualify during שחיטה, קבלה, הולכה, or זריקה. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר לִי: לֹא! אִם אָמַרְתָּ בְּשִׁינּוּי קוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבא rejects the comparison that רב פפא made in step 12 between שינוי קודש and שינוי בעלים.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: This rejects only the comparison (the proof). It does not yet give a ruling about שינוי בעלים during the year.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The comparison treats the two changes as equal. In fact, שינוי קודש has two strengths that שינוי בעלים lacks: its פסול is in the offering itself, and it applies in all ארבע עבודות.
